title_en: Honglong Industrial Co., Ltd. v. Hejiawan Station of Shanghai Railway Sub-bureau, et al. — retrial of dispute over claims for overdue cargo damage under railway freight transport contract

full_text_en:
Honglong Industrial Co., Ltd. v. Shanghai Railway Branch Hejiawan Station, et al.

— Retrial of dispute over claim for damages for overdue delivery and cargo damage under railway cargo transport contract

Retrial Petitioner: Zhuzhou North Station, Changsha Railway General Company. Domicile: Station Building, People's North Road, Zhuzhou City, Hunan Province.

Person in Charge: Yi Fusheng, Stationmaster.

Agent ad litem: Jiang Keyuan, Director of the Commodity Inspection Workshop, Zhuzhou North Station, Changsha Railway General Company.

Retrial Petitioner: Yingtan Station, Nanchang Railway Bureau. Domicile: No. 1, Dongyi Village, Yuehu District, Yingtan City, Jiangxi Province.

Person in Charge: Zhang Yingdong, Stationmaster.

Agent ad litem: Li Xiaoting, Staff Member, Freight Office, Yingtan Station, Nanchang Railway Bureau.

Agent ad litem: Yuan Demin, Attorney at Law, Nanchang Foreign-Related Economic Law Firm.

Original Appellee at Second Instance and Defendant at First Instance: Yangpu Station, Shanghai Railway Branch. Domicile: No. 4041, Zhoujiazui Road, Shanghai.

Person in Charge: Li Xiangji, Stationmaster.

Agent ad litem: Huang Shijun, Deng Laibao, Staff Members, Yangpu Station, Shanghai Railway Branch.

Opposing Party: Shanghai Honglong Industrial Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 25, Lane 141, Wenshui East Road, Shanghai.

Legal Representative: Wang Rihong, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Wu Yigang, Attorney at Law, Shanghai Sunshine Law Firm.

The opposing party Shanghai Honglong Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Honglong Company) and the original appellee at second instance and defendant at first instance Hejiawan Station, Shanghai Railway Branch (which has now been merged into Yangpu Station, Shanghai Railway Branch, with Yangpu Station exercising its rights and obligations, hereinafter referred to as Hejiawan Station), the retrial petitioners Zhuzhou North Station, Changsha Railway General Company (hereinafter referred to as Zhuzhou North Station), and Yingtan Station, Nanchang Railway Bureau (hereinafter referred to as Yingtan Station) were involved in a dispute over claims for damages for overdue delivery and cargo damage under a railway cargo transport contract. After the second-instance judgment of the Shanghai High People's Court, Zhuzhou North Station and Yingtan Station refused to accept the judgment and applied to the Supreme People's Court for retrial. The Supreme People's Court, in accordance with Article 177, Paragraph 2, and Article 183 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, decided to bring the case for trial and ordered the suspension of enforcement of the original judgment.

The Supreme People's Court found through trial:

On April 19, 1995, entrusted by Honglong Company, Guangdong Provincial Materials Storage and Transportation Company handled the consignment procedures at Guangzhou East Station for 240 iron-drum-packed TD glycerol that had been rejected by the buyer. The goods were self-loaded and self-locked into boxcar No. P632697 (60-ton capacity), with seal number 0276. The waybill filled in by the consignor recorded: 240 pieces of glycerol, weight 60 tons, cargo value RMB 60,000, insured value RMB 60,000, destination Shanghai Hejiawan Station, consignee Shanghai Honglong Industrial Co., Ltd. The freight ticket prepared by the carrier indicated a transit period of 9 days.

Boxcar No. P632697 departed from Guangzhou East Station on April 20, 1995, and arrived at Zhuzhou North Station the next day. During train marshalling operations, it was twice shunted to Baima Long Station for holding, and was not released from holding until May 18, when it returned to Zhuzhou North Station and was marshalled into a through freight train departing that same day. It arrived at Yingtan Station on the same day. During routine inspection, train inspectors found that the side bearing clearance and bolster springs on one side of the running gear of Car No. P632697 were compressed to the limit, rendering the car unfit for continued operation. The car was therefore sent to Yingtan South Station for transshipment and repair. On June 8, Yingtan South Station transshipped the cargo from Car No. P632697 onto two open wagons covered with tarpaulins. The freight record at the time of transshipment noted: Oil stains on the car floor; after inventory, 17 empty drums were found, and 7 drums had a 0.8×0.4 cm breach (new tear) in the middle section, with approximately half the contents remaining. After transshipment, the two open wagons were dispatched on June 9 and arrived at Hejiawan Station on June 14.

Consignee Honglong Company unloaded the cargo itself. The freight record at the time of unloading noted: 44 empty drums, 36 half-full drums. The outer packaging of the cargo was affixed with English labels reading "SORBITOL NEOSORB" (i.e., sorbitol, isomer 1 sorbitol), "NET 275KG" (i.e., net weight 275 kg), "Gross 296Kg" (i.e., gross weight 296 kg). There were no Chinese markings on the drums. Honglong Company sampled and weighed 10 full drums; the heaviest weighed 273 kg and the lightest 270 kg. The goods in question were subsequently subjected to an on-site visual inspection by the Shanghai Product Quality Supervision and Inspection Institute, with results: TD glycerol totaled 240 drums, of which 61 were empty and 179 were full. Among the 179 full drums, 167 were bulging. Four bulging drums were randomly sampled; gas was emitting from each, and the contents all had a fermented odor. The sampling inspection concluded: The product failed this inspection.

Separately, it was found that the batch of TD glycerol in question was produced by Jiangsu Taixing Glycerol Factory between November 5 and November 13, 1994. The enterprise standard for the product did not specify the components of TD glycerol, and stipulated a shelf life of 6 months. Entrusted by the court, the Institute of Chemistry, Chinese Academy of Sciences, tested a sample of TD glycerol taken from Taixing Glycerol Factory. The result showed: The TD glycerol sample is an aqueous solution of a mixture of polyols and polysaccharides. The most abundant component in the mixture is hexanol (also known as six-carbon alcohol sugars, such as sorbitol, mannitol, etc.), followed by six-carbon monosaccharides. On November 13, 1994, Honglong Company purchased this batch of TD glycerol at RMB 10,000/ton and shipped it to Guangdong to fulfill a contract for the sale of glycerol (glycerin) with Guangzhou Runze Co., Ltd. When unloading at Guangdong Shiweitang Station on November 16, 1994, the freight record noted: 5 drums had varying degrees of leakage; intact drums weighed 275 kg. The buyer's deputy manager, Deng Zhiqiang, stated: On December 26, 1994, Honglong Company General Manager Wang Rihong brought technicians to Guangzhou to inspect the goods and found that the odor was abnormal, there was no stickiness when tested by hand, some goods had fermented, and some drums were bulging. Because the quality did not meet specifications, the buyer demanded a return. Honglong Company decided to ship the goods back to Shanghai. By this time, the goods had been滞留 in Guangzhou for 5 months.

Honglong Company filed a lawsuit, alleging that the railway transport enterprise had engaged in rough handling, causing severe damage to the packaging; that the goods were overdue by 47 days, causing deterioration; and that the carrier was grossly negligent. It requested a judgment ordering the destination station Hejiawan Station to compensate for cargo damage and other losses totaling RMB 840,889. Shanghai Railway Transport Intermediate Court added Zhuzhou North Station and Yingtan Station as third parties. After trial, the court held: Honglong Company's allegations of rough handling and gross negligence by the carrier lacked sufficient evidence. The retention of the car by Zhuzhou North Station caused the goods to be delivered overdue and beyond their shelf life, leading to deterioration. Zhuzhou North Station had ordinary negligence and should bear liability for compensation within the insured value of the goods. Since the goods had already passed their shelf life when they arrived at Yingtan Station, and the detention and transshipment were due to overloading, Yingtan Station bore no liability for compensation. The first-instance judgment ordered Zhuzhou North Station to compensate Honglong Company for cargo damage of RMB 60,000 according to the insured value, plus overdue penalty of RMB 1,434.

Honglong Company and Zhuzhou North Station refused to accept the first-instance judgment and appealed to the Shanghai High People's Court. After trial, the court held: Zhuzhou North Station argued that due to the limited vehicle passage capacity at the Liling bottleneck, the car was retained, which constituted force majeure, and Zhuzhou North Station should not bear liability for cargo damage and breach of contract arising from the overdue delivery caused by retention. However, in fact, another shipment of TD glycerol consigned by Honglong Company the day after the consignment of the goods in question arrived in Shanghai within 8 days. Even if retention measures were necessary due to limited vehicle passage capacity, it was difficult to accept the argument that the later-shipped goods arrived earlier, and Zhuzhou North Station sought to avoid responsibility by citing retention. TD glycerol has a certain shelf life. Yingtan Station did not transship the arriving car in a timely manner, causing the TD glycerol consigned by Honglong Company to be滞留 at that station, resulting in overdue deterioration. The carrier was indeed grossly negligent and should bear full liability for compensation. Honglong Company's appeal request for compensation based on actual losses was not improper. Accordingly, the Shanghai High People's Court, applying the Ministry of Railways' regulation that "railway freight loss compensation is paid by the destination station," set aside the first-instance judgment and instead ordered Hejiawan Station to compensate Honglong Company for cargo loss of RMB 600,000.

Zhuzhou North Station's grounds for retrial application were: Because Honglong Company concealed the true name, value, and the fact that the goods already had quality problems before being shipped back, the carrier determined that this car was eligible for retention. Under conditions of limited vehicle passage capacity, the car was retained pursuant to a dispatching order. Zhuzhou North Station could not change this and should not bear responsibility for it.

Yingtan Station's grounds for retrial application were: (1) For this batch of goods to be completely fermented and deteriorated more than 20 days after the shelf life, the product quality is self-evident. Moreover, the goods were packed in used iron drums without any Chinese markings, and quality problems existed before shipment. The consignor never declared these circumstances to the carrier, causing the carrier to transport this batch of "glycerol" as ordinary goods. The consignor bears an inescapable responsibility for this. (2) Honglong Company overloaded the car, damaging it. Our station decided to transship and detain the car for repair in order to prevent a train derailment. We should not be held liable for the resulting detention of the goods.

In court trial, Honglong Company argued: (1) This is a transport contract, not a sales contract. The railway has no need to concern itself with the quality of the goods. According to Article 19 of the Railway Law, the railway should verify the packaging and weight of the goods it accepts. Since it accepted them, it should be deemed to have consented. (2) Having collected the freight, the railway is obliged to deliver the goods intact to the destination within the period stipulated in the transport contract. It cannot use transport capacity constraints as a defense against the shipper. The goods in this case were delivered 47 days overdue; the carrier was certainly grossly negligent.

Yangpu Station stated: We fully agree with the grounds for retrial of Zhuzhou North Station and Yingtan Station. After the goods arrived at the destination station, they were unloaded by Honglong Company itself and piled on an uneven open-air site. They were not moved into an indoor warehouse until several days later. The deterioration and fermentation of the goods were caused by quality problems inherent in the goods themselves. The carrier should not bear liability for compensation. Honglong Company's argument that the goods deteriorated because they were delivered beyond their shelf life is untenable.

The Supreme People's Court held:

Article 19 of the Railway Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "The consignor shall truthfully fill in the consignment note. The railway transport enterprise has the right to inspect the name, weight, and quantity of the goods and parcels filled in the note." Article 20 provides that the consignor shall package the consigned goods in accordance with national or industry packaging standards so that the goods are not damaged due to packaging during transport.

Because the contents of the waybill determine what transport measures the carrier takes to ensure the safety of the goods, the law makes the truthful filling of the waybill an obligation that the consignor must fulfill. The consignor entrusted by Honglong Company filled in the name "glycerol" on the waybill, but the actual goods consigned were TD glycerol. The value of the goods declared on the waybill was RMB 60,000, but the actual value of the entire batch was RMB 600,000. The consignor failed to fulfill the obligation of truthfully filling in the waybill.

The chemical name of glycerol is "glycerin." Its properties are relatively stable, and it has no special transport requirements. If the packaging is not tightly sealed or the shelf life is exceeded by one or two months, it will only cause the glycerol content to decrease due to moisture absorption, but not result in chemical changes. In contrast, the main chemical component of TD glycerol is hexanol. It contains more hydroxyl groups, has relatively active chemical properties, and is a substance highly susceptible to oxidation. If the outer packaging is not tightly sealed, the oxidation process will accelerate, leading to deterioration. Honglong Company used old iron drums that had previously contained isomerized sorbitol, which has a more active chemical property than hexanol, to pack and ship back the TD glycerol. This did not comply with the enterprise standard of Taixing Glycerol Factory, which requires TD glycerol to be packed in clean, dried, plastic-coated or galvanized drums, nor did it comply with the national standard for glycerol, which requires packaging in aluminum drums (with iron reinforcing frames), galvanized or resin-coated iron containers, and ensuring that the drum lids are tight, the drums are sealed, and they are leak-proof, moisture-proof, and non-absorbent. When this batch of goods was shipped from Shanghai to Guangzhou, there were already problems of leakage, some goods fermenting, and drum bulging. This indicates that the packaging damage, leakage, most drum tops bulging, and the deterioration and fermentation observed during the return shipment were fundamentally caused by the packaging being inadequate, leading to oxidation of the goods, and were not necessarily related to the overdue delivery.

Articles 8 and 10 of the "Management Measures for Insured Railway Cargo Transport" provide that full-cart load goods with an insured value exceeding RMB 500,000 should be dispatched promptly, and intermediate stops should generally not exceed 24 hours. Because the consignor entrusted by Honglong Company failed to truthfully declare the value of the goods, the carrier determined that the goods were low-value ordinary goods with no special transport requirements. Therefore, when selecting cars for retention, the decision was made to retain this car based on the principle of prioritizing ordinary goods over special goods. The goods were transported in a boxcar, loaded and locked by the consignor itself. According to Article 47(1) of the "Railway Cargo Transport Regulations" promulgated by the Ministry of Railways of the People's Republic of China in 1991, the carrier and consignor hand over based on seals; the internal condition and packaging of the goods are the responsibility of the consignor. The inspection of goods by railway transport enterprises provided for in Article 19 of the Railway Law is a right of the carrier, not an obligation. The carrier, based on the contents filled in the waybill and in accordance with transport regulations, decided to retain the car, extending the transport time and aggravating the deterioration of the goods. This was caused by the natural properties of the goods themselves and the fault of the consignor. Pursuant to Article 18, Paragraph 1, Items (2) and (3) of the Railway Law, the carrier does not bear liability for compensation.

According to the train operation diagram, Liling Station can normally pass through nearly 700 heavy cars per day. Although Liling Station is a bottleneck for railway transport, not all cars are subject to restriction in their passage. When passage capacity is limited, it is precisely by adopting retention measures for some cars to give way that the line is kept clear, allowing more subsequent cars to pass smoothly. The number of cars to be retained, the duration of retention, and the order of coupling are controlled by the train dispatcher based on traffic flow and marshalling principles, not on a first-come, first-served basis. The second-instance judgment's conclusion that, because another batch of glycerol shipped back by Honglong Company arrived within 8 days, the overdue delivery was not due to limited vehicle passage capacity at the Liling bottleneck, and thus inferring gross negligence by the carrier, was unfounded.

The transit period for the goods in this case was 9 days; they were delivered 47 days overdue. Article 16 of the Railway Law provides: "The railway transport enterprise shall transport goods, parcels, and luggage to the destination station within the period agreed upon in the contract or the period prescribed by the competent railway department under the State Council; if delivery is overdue, the railway transport enterprise shall pay a penalty." Article 18, Paragraph 5 of the "Detailed Rules for the Implementation of Railway Cargo Transport Contracts" provides that the carrier who "fails to transport the goods to the destination station within the prescribed transit period shall pay the consignee a penalty ranging from 5% to 20% of the freight collected for the batch of goods." Although Zhuzhou North Station retained the car due to capacity constraints, resulting in the overdue delivery, this still constitutes a breach of contract by the carrier, unrelated to the consignor or consignee. Zhuzhou North Station shall pay the penalty for the overdue period in accordance with the law. The allowable load of boxcar No. P632697 used by the consignor was 60 tons. The consignor shipped 240 pieces; the average gross weight of each piece should have been within 250 kg. However, the outer packaging of the goods in this case indicated a gross weight of 296 kg, and the full drums weighed an average of over 270 kg. There was indeed overloading. When Yingtan Station found that the car had been damaged due to overloading, it decided to transship and detain the car for repair to ensure railway transport safety. It should not generally be held liable for the losses caused thereby. However, Yingtan Station failed to arrange transshipment vehicles in a timely manner based on the specific circumstances and should therefore also bear liability for the overdue delivery at its station. Considering that the damage to the car was caused by the consignor's overloading, Yingtan Station's liability for breach of contract for the overdue delivery may be correspondingly reduced. In summary, the Supreme People's Court, on September 12, 2000, rendered the following judgment:

1. Set aside the second-instance civil judgment of the Shanghai High People's Court and the first-instance civil judgment of the Shanghai Railway Transport Intermediate Court;

2. Dismiss Honglong Company's claim for compensation for cargo loss;

3. The destination station, Yangpu Station, Shanghai Railway Branch, on behalf of the carrier, shall pay to Honglong Company a penalty for overdue delivery in the amount of RMB 496.84.

Court acceptance fees of RMB 30,520 for the first and second instances, and appraisal fees of RMB 3,000, shall be borne by the opposing party, Honglong Company.
